scope: Self-chat ack-echo attribution in ButlerRuntime.process (packages/textbutler/src/runtime.ts) and the conversation snapshot builder (packages/textbutler/src/reply-loop.ts): the post-compose conversation-changed recheck now attributes an incoming echo to this run's ack through relatedMessageId, matching the attribution pattern contact-habitat.ts already uses for reply followups.

rounds.design: Treat any new message id absent from both the pre-compose snapshot and this run's accepted ack ids as conversation-changed (pre-change behavior).
blockers: In a self-chat the provider re-delivers the butler's own ack as an incoming row under a fresh message id, so the ack's own echo always read as a foreign new message: every acked run in the owner self-chat cancelled as conversation-changed between ack dispatch and reply submit (observed live, run 4ef7ac99).
The echo is not an owner send, so the failure was silent: the contact saw the disclosure ack and then nothing, indistinguishable from a compose crash.

rounds.design: Carry each message's relatedMessageId in ConversationSnapshot and exempt a new id from the change check only when it relates to a journaled ack id of this same run.
blockers: Exempting by disclosure text would also excuse a contact quoting or spoofing the ack marker; relation-to-journaled-ack is structural and cannot be manufactured by message text. Fixed by keying the exemption on the provider-assigned relatedMessageId.

Exempting all related messages would let a contact reply to the ack race the reply; only relations targeting this run's accepted ack ids pass. Fixed by comparing the relation target against the run-scoped ackIds set, not the global journal.
acceptedNits: A provider that re-ids echoes without relatedMessageId still cancels — fail-safe direction, identical to the prior foreign-id treatment.

Contact replies that genuinely target the ack (reply-to) would pass the exemption only when the provider models them as a relation of the ack id; iMessage expressives do not carry relatedMessageId, so the exemption is narrower than the observed echo in practice.
The reply leg itself has the same theoretical self-echo, but no changed-check runs after the reply submit, so nothing new cancels.
rounds.verification: Live ghostget event stream shows the self-chat ack arriving as outgoing id DFC96D36 then re-landing as incoming id 32A75E0C with relatedMessageId=DFC96D36; runtime.test.ts now pins both the echo exemption and the foreign-relation cancel.
